content: 1. Fosamprenavir can increase the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis when combined with red yeast rice, as red yeast rice contains monacolin K, which is chemically identical to lovastatin. 2. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of repotrectinib by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Discontinue strong or moderate CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3-5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 3. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of ribociclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used with ribociclib, reduce the ribociclib starting dose to 400 mg/day. 4. Rifabutin decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 5. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 6. Rifapentine decreases fosamprenavir levels by increasing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of riociguat. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Monitor for signs of hypotension and reduce the riociguat dose if necessary. 8. Ritonavir increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 9. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of romidepsin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors if possible. 10. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of ruxolitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Reduce the ruxolitinib starting dose to 10 mg BID if platelet count is ≥100 x 10^9/L and a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is used concurrently. Avoid use if platelet counts are <100 x 10^9/L. 11. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of selumetinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If coadministration with strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the selumetinib dosage as per its monograph. Resume the pre-inhibitor dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for 3 elimination half-lives. 12. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of silodosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 13. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of siponimod by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining siponimod with both moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and moderate/strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. 14. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of sirolimus by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of sonidegib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining sonidegib with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 16. St. John’s Wort decreases fosamprenavir levels by inducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 17. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of suvorexant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Suvorexant is not recommended with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 18. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of tadalafil by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Stop tadalafil >24 hours before initiating a protease inhibitor (PI), restart 7 days after PI initiation at 20 mg once daily, and increase to 40 mg once daily based on tolerability. 19. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of tamoxifen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. CYP3A4 inhibition reduces tamoxifen metabolism to its active metabolite, N-desmethyl tamoxifen. 20. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of tamsulosin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 21. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of tazemetostat by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining tazemetostat with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the tazemetostat dose as per its monograph. 22. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 23. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of tofacitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Reduce the tofacitinib dose to 5 mg once daily when combined with potent CYP3A4 inhibitors. 24. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of tolvaptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 25. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of trabectedin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If a strong CYP3A inhibitor must be used short-term (e.g., <14 days), administer the inhibitor 1 week after trabectedin infusion and discontinue it the day before the next trabectedin infusion. 26. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of trazodone by inhibiting its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 27. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of triazolam by inhibiting its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 28. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of trimipramine by inhibiting its metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 29. Tucatinib increases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Avoid combining tucatinib with CYP3A substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious toxicities. If unavoidable, reduce the CYP3A substrate dose as per product labeling. 30. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of vemurafenib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of vilazodone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If intolerable adverse effects occur with moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors, reduce the vilazodone dose to 20 mg daily. 32. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of vorapaxar by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 33. Voriconazole and fosamprenavir mutually increase each other’s levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 34. Fosamprenavir and abacavir both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of abemaciclib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors increase plasma levels of abemaciclib and its metabolites, necessitating dose reduction. If the strong CYP3A4 inhibitor is discontinued, increase abemaciclib to the pre-inhibitor dose. 36. Fosamprenavir decreases the effects of acarbose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. New-onset or worsening diabetes mellitus and hyperglycemia have been reported with protease inhibitors. 37. Fosamprenavir decreases the effects of albiglutide. Use caution and monitor closely. Hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance has been reported with protease inhibitors. 38. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of almotriptan by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of alprazolam by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Aluminum hydroxide decreases fosamprenavir levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of amitriptyline by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Amobarbital decreases fosamprenavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of apalutamide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 or CYP2C8 inhibitors does not require initial dose modification, but dose reduction may be needed based on tolerability. 45. Aprepitant increases fosamprenavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Armodafinil decreases fosamprenavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Atazanavir increases fosamprenavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of bazedoxifene/conjugated estrogens by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Belzutifan decreases fosamprenavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. If coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates is unavoidable, consider increasing the substrate dose per prescribing information. 53. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. 54. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of bexarotene by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of bortezomib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Bosutinib increases fosamprenavir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of brentuximab vedotin by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Monitor patients for adverse reactions. 58. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If also combined with a strong/moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose. 59. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of bromocriptine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while budesonide decreases fosamprenavir levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely due to potential toxicity. 62. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine buccal by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely due to potential toxicity. 63. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine subdermal implant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor patients for signs of overmedication. Implant removal may be necessary if dose adjustment is not feasible. 64. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of buprenorphine long-acting injection by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor plasma levels to ensure adequacy and adjust therapy if toxicity occurs. 65. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of buspirone by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Butabarbital decreases fosamprenavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 67. Butalbital decreases fosamprenavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of cabazitaxel by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely due to potential toxicity. Avoid coadministration. 69. Fosamprenavir increases the levels or effects of calcifediol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. CYP450 inhibitors may alter vitamin D metabolism, affecting serum calcifediol levels and its conversion.
